# usd_deps: generate a USD scene's dependency list

`isaac_sim_action` fails when a scene depends on a local file that is not in
`scene` or `assets`. `usd_deps` writes that list for you, so it does not have to
be kept by hand.

```
bazel run @rules_omniverse//tools:usd_deps -- [--check] SCENE...
```

Inside this repository the target is `//tools:usd_deps`.

For each scene the tool writes a file beside it. For `stage.usda`:

```starlark
"""Generated by usd_deps from stage.usda. Do not edit."""

STAGE_DEPS = [
    "props/chair.usda",
    "textures/wood.png",
]
```

You add one load and one attribute, once:

```starlark
load(":stage_deps.bzl", "STAGE_DEPS")

isaac_sim_action(
    name = "generate",
    scene = "stage.usda",
    assets = STAGE_DEPS,
    ...
)
```

When the scene changes, run the tool again. In CI, run it with `--check`.

## Requirements

None to set up. Bazel supplies the interpreter and usd-core, and the `python3`
on `PATH` is never started: it can be any version, broken, or absent.

- `//tools:usd_deps` runs a rules_python `py_binary` on the Python 3.11
  toolchain, with usd-core 26.11 (which needs Python 3.11 or newer) from the pip
  hub `rules_omniverse_usd_deps_pip`. Its lock file,
  `tools/usd_deps_requirements_lock.txt`, pins usd-core and nothing else.
- The binary pins the Python version it needs (`python_version = "3.11"`) and the
  module registers that toolchain, so a consumer whose root module has a
  different default Python still runs the tool on 3.11.
- rules_python's default start-up script begins with `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, so
  a plain `py_binary` needs a working `python3` on `PATH` before Bazel's
  interpreter takes over. The target therefore uses rules_python's shell start-up
  (`bootstrap_impl = script`), set by the target itself. Consumers add no flag.
- `rules_python`, the Python 3.11 toolchain and that pip hub are real
  (non-dev) dependencies of the module, and nothing else new is.
  `@isaac_sim_test_pip` and `bazel_skylib` stay `dev_dependency`.
  `tools/BUILD.bazel` must not load a repository that is a `dev_dependency`,
  because consumers of the module do not have it.

`--help` works without importing `pxr`. If `pxr` cannot be imported, for example
because of a broken wheel, the tool exits non-zero with a one-line message naming
`usd-core`, not a traceback.

## Scene arguments

A relative `SCENE` is resolved against the directory `bazel run` was started
from (`BUILD_WORKING_DIRECTORY`), or the current directory when run directly.
A scene that does not exist fails, naming it. No `SCENE` is a usage error (exit 2).

## What counts as a dependency

The tool uses exactly the resolution the launcher's scene check uses. One
function, `scene_dependencies(scene)` in `omniverse/private/isaac_sim_launcher.py`,
calls `UsdUtils.ComputeAllDependencies(scene)` and sorts the answer into three
groups:

| Group | Paths |
| --- | --- |
| local | each layer's `realPath or identifier`, and each resolved asset, that is not online |
| unresolved | each unresolved path that is not online |
| online | any of those paths matching `^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]+:/` |

The launcher's `_check_scene` and `tools/usd_deps.py` both call that function,
and neither calls `ComputeAllDependencies` itself. It stays in the launcher
because the launcher is the only Python file `isaac_sim_action` gives the
container; a separate module would be a new action input.

So sublayers, references, payloads and texture asset paths are all found, and
dependencies of dependencies too, with relative paths anchored as USD anchors
them. The scene itself is never in the list, because it goes in `scene`.

## The scene's package

The scene's package is the directory of the nearest `BUILD.bazel` or `BUILD`
file, starting at the scene's own directory and going up, and not above
`BUILD_WORKSPACE_DIRECTORY` when that is set. A scene with no package fails.

A dependency is inside the package when the path USD reports is under the
package directory and no directory between them holds its own `BUILD.bazel` or
`BUILD` file. Bazel labels cannot cross into a subpackage, so a file in a
subpackage is outside. Symlinks are not resolved: a symlink in the package is a
file in the package, as it is for a Bazel label, whatever it points at.

## Output

- The file is `<stem>_deps.bzl` beside the scene, where `<stem>` is the scene's
  file name without its last extension.
- It defines one list, `<STEM>_DEPS`. `<STEM>` is the stem in upper case with
  every character other than `A-Z`, `0-9` and `_` replaced by `_`, so
  `factory.v2.usda` gives `FACTORY_V2_DEPS` in `factory.v2_deps.bzl`.
- Entries are paths relative to the package, not to the scene, sorted by plain
  string order, without duplicates.
- The bytes are exactly the following, which buildifier leaves unchanged. An
  empty list is written `STAGE_DEPS = []`.

  ```starlark
  """Generated by usd_deps from stage.usda. Do not edit."""

  STAGE_DEPS = [
      "props/chair.usda",
      "textures/wood.png",
  ]
  ```

The tool writes nothing else and never edits a BUILD file.

A stem whose name would not start with a letter, such as `1st.usda` or
`_stage.usda`, fails: a `.bzl` symbol starting with `_` cannot be loaded and one
starting with a digit is not a valid name. Two scenes on one command line that
would write the same file (`stage.usd` and `stage.usda`) also fail, naming the
file.

## Online references

An online path (`https://`, `omniverse://` and so on) is not listed and does not
fail. It is printed as `usd_deps: warning: ...`, on stderr, with the path as USD
reports it, which has one slash (`https:/example.com/robot.usd`).

## Failures

A local dependency that does not exist, or that is outside the scene's package,
fails the run with a non-zero exit. The message lists every such file, for every
scene on the command line, not just the first. All scenes are checked before
anything is written, so a failed run writes nothing and leaves existing files alone.

## Running twice

Running the tool again on an unchanged scene changes nothing: a file that already
has the right bytes is not rewritten, so its modification time stays the same.

## --check

`--check` writes nothing. It exits 0 when every scene's `.bzl` file has exactly
the bytes the tool would write. Otherwise it exits non-zero and lists, for each
stale file, its path and the entries to add and remove. Entries that are correct
are not listed. A missing file is stale. A file with the right list but other
bytes, such as a hand edit, is stale too. The failures above also fail `--check`.
Online references still only warn.
